messages:
support-nora: incoming escalation from CSMs — multiple customers reporting 500s + timeouts on hosted endpoints since ~08:45 UTC. endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat/stream. customers: acme-co, syntax-ai. opening thread to coordinate. :rotating_light:
jamie-oncall: looking at prod dashboards now, 5xx rate jumped at 08:42 on the canary pool, overall 5xx -> 7.8% for a 10m window. latency p95 up from 180ms -> 1.2s. canary hosts only.
mattg: fyi i flipped a config on the canary at 08:40 — "enable-batch-prefetch=true" to try prefetching KV-cache for long-context workloads. rolling to 10% canary.
ops_liz: hmm that matches timing. any auth errors in the logs or just upstream 500s?
alin: logs show repeated "gateway: kvcache miss panic" in runtime on canary instances, stacktrace points to prefetch path. also a few 401s but likely noise. sample log: ```ERROR runtime: prefetch failed: index out of range at runtime/prefetch.go:142\nREQ id=abc123 route=x-rw-route:canary```. 
support-nora: acme-co reporting client-side retries, seeing token refresh flow failing intermittently. they say their billing meters also saw double-counted partial tokens. ticket numbers attached: SUPPORT-4821, SUPPORT-4822.
support-bot: created internal tickets: INT-5023 linked -> SUPPORT-4821, SUPPORT-4822. notifying customer success.
jamie-oncall: can we quickly disable the prefetch flag on canary? mattg can you toggle? also need to start rollback plan if toggling doesn't remediate immediately.
mattg: running toggle now: `deployctl set-config --scope=canary enable-batch-prefetch=false` — will post output.
deploy-bot: executed by mattg at 08:56 UTC. change queued to canary pool (10 hosts).
ops_liz: metric check in 30s pls.
jamie-oncall: also open question: why did prefetch touch auth flow? my hunch: prefetch thread reuses request context and clears header and causes mid-request auth refresh -> 401 turned into 500. we should search for header mutation in prefetch code.
sophiadev: adding a quick smoke repro for devs: curl to canary w/ header x-rw-route:canary and long context payload, repeat 50 concurrent -> will share script.```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "x-rw-route: canary" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2","input":"...long context..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
jamie-oncall: metrics after toggle: 60s in and 5xx dropped from 7.8% -> 0.9% on canary, p95 latency back to 220ms. looks like toggle mitigated.
ops_liz: great — still need coordinated rollback + postmortem. mattg please roll the canary change back in control plane and mark the flag default false until patch.
mattg: initiating rollback to previous config + will stop canary rollout: `deployctl rollback --to=canary-2026-03-17-0800`
deploy-bot: rollback job started by mattg, job id rb-179999-09. estimated 4m.
alin: collecting debug traces and error samples to attach to Git issue. will grep for "prefetch" and "header" in 08:30-09:10 UTC window.
support-nora: I'll update customers with ETA ~10-15m and explain we rolled back a canary config, apologies for the noise. include workaround: no changes required on client side.
sophiadev: opened GH issue: redwood/runtime#6789 with logs, traces, and repro steps. assigning to runtime team for patch.
jamie-oncall: follow-up action items: 1) revert canary flag default to false, 2) add unit test for header preservation in prefetch path, 3) add canary health gate that watches 5xx + auth-failure deltas, 4) communicate to CS about potential double-metering and billing review. please ack.
mattg: acked. i'll keep monitoring until rollback completes.
ops_liz: monitoring alert: acme-co errors trending down. their CS says they're back to normal. closing escalation after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
